l4_steps.name: Receive cargo booking and AWB data
l4_steps.input: Air Waybill (AWB), shipper booking request, commodity declaration
l4_steps.output: Booking record created in cargo management system
l4_steps.kpi: Acceptance processing time ≤15 min per shipment
l4_steps.pain_point: Paper-based AWBs delay IATA e-freight compliance; IATA eAWB mandate targets 100% adoption by 2026 but shipper readiness lags at ~68% globally

l4_steps.name: Validate AWB, weight, dimensions, and piece count
l4_steps.input: Physical cargo presented at acceptance counter, AWB data
l4_steps.output: Validated weight/dimension record; discrepancy notice if mismatch
l4_steps.kpi: AWB discrepancy rate ≤2%; re-weigh resolution ≤10 min
l4_steps.pain_point: Weight/dimension discrepancy between booked and actual triggers load plan recalculation in SkyMAX; late changes within 2h of STD cause cascading W&B revisions

l4_steps.name: Screen shipment for dangerous goods compliance
l4_steps.input: Commodity code, shipper's DG declaration, MSDS where applicable
l4_steps.output: DG acceptance confirmation or rejection notice with IATA DGR citation
l4_steps.kpi: Undeclared DG detection rate = 100%; DG non-compliance rejection logged within 5 min
l4_steps.pain_point: Undeclared lithium batteries and aerosols remain the #1 air cargo safety risk; IATA DGR 64th Edition tightens Section II battery limits, requiring agent retraining each Jan cycle

l4_steps.name: Submit ACAS pre-screening data for US-bound cargo
l4_steps.input: AWB data, commodity details, shipper/consignee identifiers
l4_steps.output: ACAS submission confirmation; Do Not Load (DNL) or cleared status from CBP
l4_steps.kpi: ACAS submission ≥4h before departure per 19 CFR 122.48a; CBP response latency typically <2 min
l4_steps.pain_point: Late ACAS submission or CBP DNL response with <1h to departure forces cargo offload, disrupting finalised load plan and triggering FFM amendment; no automated retry on CBP system timeout

l4_steps.name: Physically screen cargo via X-ray or ETD
l4_steps.input: Accepted and DG-cleared shipment presented at screening station
l4_steps.output: Screened cargo with TSA/TCAS security clearance label
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of cargo screened before loading per TSA 12-5 CCSF programme; throughput ≥600 kg/h per lane
l4_steps.pain_point: Dense or opaque shipments (machinery, consolidated freight) require manual ETD swab resolution, creating bottleneck at peak build-up windows (02:00–05:00 for early banks); insufficient overnight staffing at secondary airports

l4_steps.name: Assign screened cargo to flight and ULD position
l4_steps.input: Screened shipment data, aircraft load plan from load control, ULD inventory
l4_steps.output: ULD assignment record with build-up instructions and position code
l4_steps.kpi: ULD utilisation ≥85% by volume; assignment issued ≥3h before STD
l4_steps.pain_point: Last-minute passenger IRROP (flight cancellation/diversion) displaces belly cargo capacity, requiring full re-manifest of 15–40 shipments within 30 min with no automated re-optimisation tool in most legacy CMS configurations

l4_steps.name: Build ULD, palletise cargo, and apply labels
l4_steps.input: Build-up instructions, cargo, ULD/pallet, netting, and tiedown equipment
l4_steps.output: Completed ULD with IATA ULD tag, gross weight, and content manifest
l4_steps.kpi: Build-up accuracy (correct ULD manifest) ≥98%; ULD gross weight tolerance ±0.5% of declared
l4_steps.pain_point: Manual pallet build without automated real-time feed to weight-and-balance system means errors (overweight, CG shift) are only discovered at aircraft hold door, causing ramp delay averaging 18 min per incident

l4_steps.name: Generate and transmit final cargo manifest (FFM)
l4_steps.input: Completed ULD manifest records, AWB data, flight details
l4_steps.output: FFM Cargo-IMP message transmitted to destination station, customs, and ground handler
l4_steps.kpi: FFM transmitted ≥45 min before STD per IATA Cargo-IMP MSG standard; retransmission on amendment ≤5 min
l4_steps.pain_point: Integration gaps between CMS and PSS mean late passenger rebooking changes (affecting belly payload) trigger manual FFM amendments; automated reconciliation missing in non-NDC-integrated stations

l4_steps.name: Transport ULDs and bulk cargo to aircraft ramp
l4_steps.input: Ramp movement instruction, airside vehicle assignment, ULD ready notification
l4_steps.output: ULD delivered to aircraft position on time; vehicle movement logged
l4_steps.kpi: Cargo at aircraft ≥30 min before STD; ramp vehicle utilisation ≥80%
l4_steps.pain_point: Airside congestion at hub airports (multiple simultaneous narrow-body turns) causes sequencing conflicts between cargo dollies, fuel bowsers, and catering trucks; no real-time airside traffic management at most regional stations

l4_steps.name: Load cargo into aircraft hold per load instruction report
l4_steps.input: Load Instruction Report (LIR) from load control, ULDs and bulk cargo on ramp
l4_steps.output: Completed loading; signed LIR returned to load control; actual weights confirmed
l4_steps.kpi: Loading completion ≥15 min before STD; W&B CG deviation ≤2% of planned; LIR sign-off accuracy 100%
l4_steps.pain_point: Bulk cargo dimension inconsistencies discovered at hold door during loading trigger manual re-sequencing; Jeppesen LoadPlanner does not auto-update when actual weights deviate >50 kg from planned, requiring crew notification and possible taxi-back

l4_steps.name: Offload cargo from arriving aircraft hold
l4_steps.input: Aircraft arrival confirmation, inbound load manifest (FWB/FFM from origin)
l4_steps.output: Offloaded ULDs and bulk cargo staged on ramp with position labels
l4_steps.kpi: ULD offload complete ≤35 min after chocks-on; bulk hold clear ≤25 min
l4_steps.pain_point: Combi aircraft and wide-body mixed-class configurations require sequential hold access, extending ground time; misrouted ULDs from origin (wrong station label) discovered only at offload, requiring urgent re-manifest and re-tender

l4_steps.name: Break down inbound ULDs and scan all pieces
l4_steps.output: Individual shipment scan records; discrepancy report if count/condition mismatch
l4_steps.kpi: Breakdown and scan complete ≤60 min after offload; discrepancy rate ≤1%; cargo claim initiation ≤15 min of confirmed shortage
l4_steps.pain_point: ULD damage (torn nets, cracked pallets) discovered at breakdown delays customs release and inflates cargo claims cost; CHAMP exception workflow requires manual supervisor override, adding 20–45 min to resolution when supervisor unavailable overnight

l4_steps.name: Transmit arrival notices to consignees and forwarders
l4_steps.input: Breakdown scan records, AWB consignee and notify-party contact data
l4_steps.output: Arrival Notices (ANs) transmitted via EDI/email to all notified parties
l4_steps.kpi: Arrival notice sent ≤2h after breakdown; automated AN rate ≥95% of AWBs with complete contact data
l4_steps.pain_point: Incomplete or missing consignee contact data in AWB (common with e-commerce fulfilment shipments) prevents automated notification; manual agent intervention required, increasing dwell time and risk of exceeding free storage period

l4_steps.name: File customs entry and e-manifest for inbound cargo
l4_steps.input: AWB, commodity data, commercial invoice, country of origin certificate
l4_steps.output: Customs entry filed; Movement Reference Number (MRN) or CBP release reference received
l4_steps.kpi: Customs pre-clearance filing ≥2h before aircraft arrival per EU ICS2 and CBP advance cargo rules; entry acceptance rate ≥97%
l4_steps.pain_point: Incomplete commercial invoices from e-commerce shippers (missing HS codes, undervalued goods) cause customs holds and demurrage charges; ICS2 Phase 3 (2024) adds 6-digit HS code mandate that many SME shippers are not yet compliant with

l4_steps.name: Present cargo for customs physical examination if selected
l4_steps.input: CBP or customs authority examination order; cargo held in bonded warehouse
l4_steps.output: Cargo presented at examination bay; examination result recorded
l4_steps.kpi: Cargo presented at examination bay ≤4h of exam order; examination completion ≤8h for non-complex shipments
l4_steps.pain_point: Random and targeted exam selection (10–15% of shipments at major US gateways) creates unpredictable delay and bonded storage cost; no SLA from CBP on exam completion time, causing consignee escalations and missed just-in-time delivery windows

l4_steps.name: Release and deliver cargo to consignee upon clearance
l4_steps.input: Customs release confirmation, consignee photo ID and delivery order
l4_steps.output: Signed delivery receipt; cargo released from airline/handler custody; AWB closed
l4_steps.kpi: Dwell time ≤24h for general cargo; ≤4h for perishables and pharmaceuticals (IATA CEIV Pharma benchmark); delivery receipt accuracy 100%
l4_steps.pain_point: Free storage period expiry (typically 24–48h depending on carrier tariff) triggers demurrage charges averaging $0.50–$1.50/kg/day; consignee no-shows spike on weekends and public holidays without automated SMS/email reminder integration in CHAMP delivery module
